summary: Podes (Ancient Greek: Ποδής) is son of Eetion and a wealthy Trojan ally whom Hector honours as a welcome companion at the feast. Menelaus kills him in the fight over Patroclus' body. Wikipedia treats him as brother of Andromache; Iliad 6 has Achilles slay Andromache's seven brothers — a contradiction left unresolved.

sections.heading: Companion of Hector
paragraphs: In Iliad 17 Podes son of Eetion stands among the Trojans over Patroclus. Hector values him above the people as a feast-companion; fair-haired Menelaus smites him through the belt as he starts to flee.

Athenaeus later glosses "feast friend" toward parasite and flatterer, reading Menelaus' belly-wound as symbolic. Readers who identify his father with Andromache's Eetion of Thebe Hypoplakia must still reckon with Andromache's claim that Achilles already killed her brothers.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (podes-eetionid) is the Iliadic son of Eetion alone. The linked father node is eetion-cilicia; do not collapse him into unrelated Podes namesakes outside the Patroclus fight.
